provenance.instrument: East Manchester Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 255 Zoning, Ord. No. 2006-3, amended in its entirety 6-12-2007 by Ord. No. 2007-2, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 EA1085, Township of East Manchester, York County (255-6A(1) 'the Township of East Manchester, York County, Pennsylvania'). District use lists and lot area and bulk tables are text in Article III. The two attachments are sign charts (Chart A permanent signs, Chart B temporary signs). Floodplain rules are in Chapter 108, the riparian buffer in Chapter 199. New Laws: none
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 04-14-2026.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.' The definitions carry Ord. No. 2026-2 of 4-8-2026
checks: ADU: 'In all districts where residential uses are permitted, and subject to the requirements of the applicable district, ADUs shall be permitted' (255-21D, Ord. No. 2025-5). An ADU is 'A dwelling unit added to, or created within, a single-family dwelling', may not be sold apart from the house, and may be lived in only by 'a person related to the principal dwelling unit owner by blood, marriage, or legal adoption, or persons providing care to the principal dwelling unit owner(s)' (255-90)

The ADU residents must apply for and renew each year an ADU occupancy permit, on proof that they are related to the owner of the house. Within six months after the ADU resident moves out, or after the permit lapses, the owner must turn the ADU back into part of the house (255-21D(2), (3))

Size: the lesser of 900 sq ft or 30% of the total floor area of the dwelling (255-21D(1)). 255-42 sets 900 sq ft of livable floor area for a dwelling unit and 400 sq ft (300 sq ft for one person) for conversion apartments. Read as a floor for an ADU, the 900 sq ft would leave room only for a unit of exactly 900 sq ft in a house of 3,000 sq ft or more, and the 30% cap could never apply. A statute is read to give effect to all its provisions and not to reach an absurd result (1 Pa.C.S. 1921(a), 1922(1)), and 255-21D (Ord. No. 2025-5) is the later and specific rule. So the tool does not bar a smaller house on 255-42. Ask the zoning officer which minimum applies to an ADU

The house must keep the look of a single-family dwelling (255-21D(7)). A unit below grade needs emergency egress under the Uniform Construction Code (255-21D(5)). If the ADU brings the bedrooms served by a septic system to four or more, the Sewage Enforcement Officer must inspect and approve the system (255-21D(6))

Parking: 'One additional off-street parking space' for the ADU (255-21D(4)). A house needs one space for each 1/2 dwelling unit, which is two spaces (255-58E). Where Article IV and the parking table differ, Article IV prevails (255-58D). The table 'applies only to new construction and to the enlarged sections to any additions' (255-58E Note 1), so an existing house with fewer than two spaces may not need to add them. Spaces are at least 10 ft by 20 ft on the same lot (255-58A)

CO and A: 'Total Number of Dwelling Units Permitted (including those existing)' is one on a tract of up to 10 acres (gross area as of 1-1-2006), and two plus one per added 10 acres above that. 'Each dwelling unit shall be located on an individual lot' (255-9E, 255-10E). That last rule holds at any tract size, so even a large tract with units left in its count needs a lot for each unit. These read as barring an ADU there, while 255-21D allows ADUs in all districts where residential uses are permitted. Ask the zoning officer
C and I: 'Dwellings' are expressly prohibited (255-16D(1), 255-17E(1)), so there is no single-family dwelling to add an ADU to

Each lot gets one principal use and one principal building (255-8A(6), 255-20, district use lists). A unit in a separate building is not an ADU under the definition. 'Any use not specifically allowed elsewhere in this chapter shall be allowed by special exception in the district or districts where, and to the extent that, similar uses are permitted or allowed by special exception' (255-19, also 255-8A(4)). A unit in a detached building might be heard by the Zoning Hearing Board as a use similar to an ADU. Against that reading stand the one principal use and building rule and, in CO and A, the rule that each dwelling unit has its own lot. Not settled. C and I expressly prohibit dwellings, so this does not open a path there

Residential conversion of an existing one-family dwelling to two or more units: special exception in R-2 and R-3, by right in AO and V. The lot needs at least 60% of the district minimum lot area for each unit created. The building must have had 1,000 sq ft of livable floor area on the chapter's effective date plus 600 sq ft for each added unit, with no change to the outside except as building codes require, and 1.5 parking spaces per unit (255-33). No family rule

Duplex dwellings are by right in R-2, R-3, AO and V (255-12B(2), 255-13B(2), 255-14B(2), 255-15B(2)). That is a path for a new two-unit building. Turning the existing house into two units is a residential conversion (255-33, 255-90 'Residential conversion'), a special exception in R-2 and R-3. An ADU inside the house also fits the words of a residential conversion, but 255-21D is the later and specific rule for an ADU

Floodplain (Chapter 108, 255-18): a land use permit is needed for any construction or development in the township (108-3A, 108-5). In the floodway any increase in flood heights is prohibited and new construction needs a DEP permit (108-16A). In FE and FA areas 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless a permit is obtained from DEP' (108-16C(1)). New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation (the 100-year flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft), and a fully enclosed space below it is prohibited (108-17A, C(1), 108-34). Work of 50% or more of market value is a substantial improvement, and work under 50% 'shall be elevated and/or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible' (108-29C, D). Manufactured homes are prohibited in the floodway and within 50 ft of the top of bank in FA and FE areas (108-21A, B). No part of an on-site sewage system may be in the floodplain except in strict compliance with state and local rules (108-18C(3)). A nonconforming structure in the floodplain may not be expanded in a way that would increase flooding (255-72B). The Township may grant waivers for exceptional hardship (108-30, 108-31), and the Zoning Hearing Board hears variances from Chapter 108 (255-86B(5)), but none in the floodway that would raise the 100-year flood elevation (255-86B(10)(c)[1])

Riparian Buffer Zone (Chapter 199): along a perennial stream, a spring or a watercourse whose drainage area exceeds 75 acres, no disturbance of vegetation and soil within 15 ft of the top of bank, and in the next 35 ft (or to the 100-year floodplain if wider) only uses allowed in the floodplain (199-18A(1), (2)). Where the drainage area is less than 75 acres the zone is the 15 ft strip alone (199-18B). The small project exemptions of 199-8 reach only peak rate control and the stormwater site plan, not 199-18, so the zone reaches a house addition. An addition with up to 750 sq ft of new impervious area (counted since 1-10-2006) needs no stormwater site plan (199-8A)

Nonconforming lot: a single-family dwelling may be built on a lot of record irrespective of its area or width. The side yards together need not exceed 30% of the lot width (each at least 10%) and the rear yard need not exceed 20% of the depth (at least 10 ft) (255-71). A noncomplying building may be enlarged if no new nonconformity is created (255-70B)

Front yards: a single-family or duplex dwelling need not be set back farther than the average of the two existing dwellings with the greatest setbacks within 200 ft on each side, on the same side of the street, in the same block and district (255-48)
R-3: every use must be served by both public sewer and public water, and private septic and wells are prohibited (255-13E)

Accessory structures may be prefabricated, but not built and titled under the Pennsylvania Vehicle Code (255-21). The ADU is added to or made within the house, so this matters only for a separate building
provenance.notes: Zoning office: East Manchester Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-17. Read: 255-1 to 255-18 (chapter print view), 255-19, 255-20, 255-21, 255-27, 255-33, 255-42, 255-48, 255-58, Article VII (255-67 to 255-72), 255-76, 255-86, 255-90 up to 'Short-term rental', Chapter 108 from 108-1 to 108-31, 199-8, 199-18 and code searches. Not read: 255-18.1 (Data Center Overlay), 255-22 to 255-26, 255-28 to 255-32, 255-34 to 255-41, 255-43 to 255-47, 255-49 to 255-57.3, Article VI, 255-59 to 255-61, 255-73 to 255-75, 255-77 to 255-85, 255-87 to 255-89, 255-90 after 'Short-term rental', 255-91, 108-32, 108-33 and 199-5. Open points: which minimum unit size applies to an ADU (255-42 against 255-21D(1), read as a condition, not a bar), whether the CO and A dwelling unit limits bar an ADU, whether 30% is of the house before or after the unit is made, and whether 255-19 opens a special exception for a unit in a detached building.

term.note: 'A dwelling unit added to, or created within, a single-family dwelling that provides basic requirements for living, sleeping, eating, cooking and sanitation'

status.note: ADUs 'shall be permitted' in all districts where residential uses are permitted, by zoning permit. Only a relative of the owner of the house, or a person caring for the owner, may live in the unit

scope_districts.note: 'In all districts where residential uses are permitted'. Single-family dwellings are permitted by right in CO, A, R-1, R-2, R-3, AO and V

path.note: 'ADUs shall be permitted subject to the following the following requirements'. A zoning permit, with an ADU occupancy permit that the residents renew each year

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the hardship findings of 255-86B(10)(a). No bar on a use variance

value.name: Residential conversion (R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: Conversion of an existing one-family dwelling to a two-family or larger dwelling. The lot needs at least 60% of the district minimum lot area for each dwelling unit created (with public sewer and water, 9,000 sq ft per unit in R-2 and 4,800 sq ft per unit in R-3). The building must have had 1,000 sq ft of livable floor area on the chapter's effective date, plus 600 sq ft for each added unit. Each unit has a full kitchen, toilet and bath. No change to the outside except as building or housing codes require. 1.5 off-street parking spaces per unit. No family rule. The Zoning Hearing Board decides on the standards of 255-86D

requires.condition: An existing one-family dwelling to convert
1,000 sq ft of livable floor area for the first unit plus 600 sq ft for the second, held on the chapter's effective date

value.note: A house divided into units, not an ADU. The lot figure counts 60% of the district minimum for each of the two units, which reads as 18,000 sq ft in R-2 and 9,600 sq ft in R-3 with public sewer and water. Another reading counts only the added unit. An ADU inside the house also fits the words of a residential conversion, but the ADU section is the later and specific rule for an ADU

value.name: Residential conversion (AO, V)
value.conditions: Conversion of an existing one-family dwelling to a two-family or larger dwelling. The lot needs at least 60% of the district minimum lot area for each dwelling unit created (4,800 sq ft per unit with public sewer and water). The building must have had 1,000 sq ft of livable floor area on the chapter's effective date, plus 600 sq ft for each added unit. Each unit has a full kitchen, toilet and bath. No change to the outside except as building or housing codes require. 1.5 off-street parking spaces per unit. No family rule

requires.condition: An existing one-family dwelling to convert
1,000 sq ft of livable floor area for the first unit plus 600 sq ft for the second, held on the chapter's effective date

value.note: A house divided into units, not an ADU. In V without public sewer and water the district minimum is one acre, so the lot needs 52,272 sq ft for two units. An ADU inside the house also fits the words of a residential conversion, but the ADU section is the later and specific rule for an ADU

value.name: Duplex dwelling (R-2, R-3, AO, V)
value.conditions: A detached building for not more than two families. With public water and sewer the lot is 20,000 sq ft and 100 ft wide in R-2, 10,000 sq ft and 80 ft wide in R-3 and AO, and 10,000 sq ft and 100 ft wide in V. Without them it is 45,000 sq ft and 200 ft wide in R-2 and V. R-3 requires public sewer and water for every use. Two parking spaces per unit
value.section: 255-12B(2), D, 255-13B(2), D, 255-14B(2), D, 255-15B(2), D, 255-90 'Dwelling, duplex', 'Residential conversion'
value.note: A new two-unit building, not a change to the existing house. Each lot gets one principal building (255-8A(6)), so the duplex would take the place of the house

requires.condition: A new building for two units. Turning the existing house into two units is a residential conversion instead

zoning_districts.note: Districts where residential uses are permitted

building_types.note: The ADU is added to or made within a single-family dwelling, which the code defines as 'A detached building designed for or used exclusively for residence purposes by one family'

historic_bypass.note: No historic district or historic path was found in the parts read

value.condition: In CO and A the total number of dwelling units on a tract, counting those existing, is one up to 10 acres (gross area as of 1-1-2006), and two plus one per added 10 acres above that. 'Each dwelling unit shall be located on an individual lot', at any tract size. The ADU rule is 'subject to the requirements of the applicable district', so these limits read as barring an ADU on a house lot here.

disputed_by.note: 255-21D permits ADUs 'In all districts where residential uses are permitted', which names CO and A. Whether an accessory unit counts toward the district's dwelling unit limit is not settled

value.condition: 255-42 sets 900 sq ft of livable floor area for a dwelling unit and 400 sq ft (300 sq ft for one person) for conversion apartments. With the ADU cap of 900 sq ft or 30% of the house, whichever is less, ask the zoning officer which minimum applies to an ADU. The 900 sq ft floor would leave room only in a house of 3,000 sq ft or more, and the later ADU section reads as setting the unit's own size (1 Pa.C.S. 1921(a), 1922(1)).
The appearance of the house must remain that of a single-family dwelling, for any ADU form.
In R-3 every use must be served by both public sewer and public water. Private septic systems and wells are prohibited.

In the FE or FA floodplain areas 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless a permit is obtained from DEP'.

In the Floodplain Overlay any construction or development needs a land use permit. In the floodway any increase in flood heights is prohibited and new construction needs a DEP permit. New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure need the lowest floor, basement included, at or above the regulatory flood elevation (the 100-year flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft), and a fully enclosed space below it is prohibited. Work of 50% or more of market value is a substantial improvement. Work under 50% must be elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible.

Riparian Buffer Zone: along a perennial stream, a spring or a watercourse whose drainage area exceeds 75 acres, no disturbance of vegetation and soil within 15 ft of the top of bank, and in the next 35 ft, or to the 100-year floodplain if that is wider, only uses allowed in the floodplain. Where the drainage area is less than 75 acres the zone is the 15 ft strip alone. The small project exemptions do not reach this rule.

A single-family or duplex dwelling need not be set back farther from the street than the average of the two existing dwellings with the greatest setbacks within 200 ft on each side, on the same side of the street, in the same block and district.

types_allowed.note: 'A dwelling unit added to, or created within, a single-family dwelling'. A unit over an attached garage that is part of the house is an addition

types_not_addressed.note: The definition names only a unit added to or made within the house, so a garage attached to the house counts as part of it and garage conversion here means a detached garage. A unit in a separate building is not named, and each lot gets one principal use (255-20). A use not specifically allowed is a special exception where similar uses are allowed (255-19), which might let the Zoning Hearing Board hear a unit in a detached building. Not settled

max_sqft.note: 'The maximum area of the ADU shall be the lesser of: (a) Nine hundred square feet; or (b) Thirty percent of the total floor area of the dwelling.'

max_share_of_house.note: 'Thirty percent of the total floor area of the dwelling', whichever is less. Whether the dwelling's floor area counts the unit is not said

occupancy.value: A person related to the owner of the house by blood, marriage or legal adoption, or a person providing care to the owner. The residents apply for and renew an ADU occupancy permit each year, and the unit must be turned back into part of the house within six months after the resident leaves or the permit lapses.

owner_occupancy.note: No rule that the owner live on the lot. The ADU resident must be related to the owner of the house, or care for the owner

max_adus.note: The code gives no count. The definition speaks of 'A dwelling unit' added to the house

sale_apart_allowed.note: 'Accessory units may not be subdivided or otherwise segregated in ownership from the principle dwelling unit and use'

spaces_required.note: 'One additional off-street parking space.' Article IV prevails over the parking table (255-58D)

total_on_site.note: Two spaces for the house (one space for each 1/2 dwelling unit) and one for the ADU. The table applies only to new construction and to the enlarged sections of additions (255-58E Note 1), so an existing house with fewer than two spaces may need only the ADU's space
